name: Antigua and Barbuda
headline: Antigua and Barbuda: +3.0% growth in 2025, 1.4% inflation, debt 70% of GDP
sections: Antigua and Barbuda is a $2.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 191st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.0% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $36K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 2.4% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 1.4% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.5% in 2022.
Gross government debt is 70% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 101% in 2020. The general government balance is +3.2% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is −11.6% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 118% of GDP (2022), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 12.1% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 59% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 77.8 years (2024). Population: 105 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
